charts.title: 01_runtime_bars
charts.caption: Wall-clock for the same SBML composite under the Python process-bigraph engine vs the Rust viva-core engine, at two simulated horizons. A single heavy libroadrunner process dominates, so the engine swap moves only framework overhead (within ~10%); the two engines produce bit-identical results (max abs diff 0.0 across all 9 observables).

charts.title: 02_model_runtime_48h
charts.caption: Wall-clock to run one matched 48 h sepsis simulation, real BioGears 8.2.0 engine vs the SBML/Tellurium extraction (committed run metadata, meta.wall_s). The extraction is modestly faster — 2.15 h vs 3.35 h (1.56×) at mild infection and 2.81 h vs 3.38 h (1.20×) at severe — but not orders of magnitude, because integrating the stiff 91-state ODE in roadrunner is itself heavy (see study 06). This is the model-vs-model comparison relevant to large virtual-patient sweeps; it is a different axis from the composition-engine swap (process-bigraph vs viva-core), which is bit-identical and overhead-only.

charts.title: Model-vs-model 48 h wall-clock: real engine vs SBML extraction (SBML modestly faster)
charts.caption: Wall-clock to run one matched 48 h sepsis simulation, real BioGears 8.2.0 engine vs the SBML/Tellurium extraction (committed run metadata, meta.wall_s). The extraction is modestly faster — 2.15 h vs 3.35 h (1.56×) at mild infection and 2.81 h vs 3.38 h (1.20×) at severe — but not orders of magnitude, because integrating the stiff 91-state ODE in roadrunner is itself heavy (see study 06). This is the model-vs-model comparison relevant to large virtual-patient sweeps; it is a different axis from the composition-engine swap (process-bigraph vs viva-core), which is bit-identical and overhead-only.
